facts.raw_span: intractable mucocutaneous lesions that had been evolving for 10 years
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes were palpable
Small bullae, erosions, and crusts were present on the lower lip
Erosions with epithelized mucosa were observed in the oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions were present on the face, trunk, and extremities
Chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography showed no abnormalities
Gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results identified no abnormalities
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis and superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No obvious deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 to either the epithelial cell surface or the basement membrane zone
IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin (210 kDa) and periplakin (190 kDa)
Negative for Dsg1, Dsg3, and BP180 16th noncollagenous domain
Negative for BP230, type VII collagen, and desmocollins 1 to 3

concepts.why: The presence of mucocutaneous lesions, skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and numerous neutrophils, and IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin support this diagnosis.
The presence of flaccid bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin and mucous membranes, along with the absence of other systemic symptoms, support this diagnosis.
The presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin, along with the skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis.
The presence of linear IgA deposits on the skin biopsy and the clinical presentation of bullae and erosions support this diagnosis.
The presence of papulovesicular lesions, along with the skin biopsy revealing neutrophils and superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis.
The presence of target lesions, along with the skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis.
The presence of mucocutaneous lesions, along with the skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis.
The presence of widespread skin necrosis, along with the skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Intractable mucocutaneous lesions suggest an autoimmune or chronic condition, which could be related to paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F03: Mucocutaneous lesions are a hallmark of pemphigus and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F04: Oral mucosa involvement is common in pemphigus and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F05: Skin lesions on the face, trunk, and extremities are consistent with pemphigus and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F08: Spongiosis and neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis are characteristic of pemphigus and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F10: IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin are specific for paraneoplastic pemphigus.
